questions.question_text: A blood sample clots normally, but its oxygen-carrying capacity is markedly reduced. Which formed element is most directly deficient?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin within erythrocytes transports most oxygen in blood; platelets mediate clotting and leukocytes defend against infection.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person with blood group AB (Rh-positive) is considered a universal recipient for red-cell transfusion under the ABO/Rh system because the person's plasma normally lacks which antibodies?
questions.explanation: AB plasma normally has neither anti-A nor anti-B, so ABO red-cell antigens A and B are not attacked. Rh matching still matters clinically; Rh positivity alone does not make anti-D universally absent in every circumstance.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly traces a red blood cell from the right ventricle until it returns to the left atrium?
questions.option_a: Pulmonary artery → lung capillaries → pulmonary veins
questions.option_c: Pulmonary vein → lung capillaries → pulmonary artery
questions.explanation: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary artery to lung capillaries; oxygenated blood returns by pulmonary veins to the left atrium.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than that of the right ventricle?
questions.option_a: It receives blood directly from the lungs
questions.option_b: It must generate pressure to send blood through the systemic circulation
questions.option_c: It stores oxygenated blood between heartbeats
questions.option_d: It prevents blood from entering the pulmonary artery
questions.explanation: The left ventricle pumps blood through the whole body and therefore needs a thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle, which pumps only to the lungs.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A blockage occurs in the coronary arteries. Which tissue is directly deprived of its usual oxygen-rich blood supply?
questions.explanation: Coronary arteries supply oxygenated blood to the myocardium; their obstruction can cause myocardial ischaemia or infarction.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which feature most directly enables capillaries to exchange gases and dissolved substances efficiently with tissues?
questions.option_b: A single-cell-thick wall and extensive branching
questions.option_d: A wide lumen with rapid turbulent flow
questions.explanation: Thin walls and a large, branching surface bring blood close to tissue cells and permit diffusion; muscular thickness is characteristic of arteries.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes pulmonary arteries from most other arteries in an adult human?
questions.option_a: They carry blood away from the heart but usually carry deoxygenated blood
questions.option_b: They carry blood toward the heart and usually carry oxygenated blood
questions.option_c: They carry blood away from the heart and always carry oxygenated blood
questions.option_d: They connect the vena cava directly to the lungs
questions.explanation: Arteries are defined by carrying blood away from the heart, not by oxygen content. Pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In a healthy adult, the first heart sound is produced mainly when which valves close?
questions.explanation: The first heart sound (S1) is associated with closure of the atrioventricular valves at the start of ventricular systole.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A defect allows blood to pass between the right and left ventricles. What is the most direct consequence of this abnormal opening?
questions.option_a: Complete separation of the two blood circuits is compromised
questions.option_b: Blood can no longer enter either atrium
questions.option_c: The vena cava becomes an artery
questions.option_d: The pulmonary veins stop returning blood to the heart
questions.explanation: A ventricular septal opening permits mixing or shunting between the two sides of the heart and disrupts normal separation of pulmonary and systemic circulation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which component is the principal first-line cellular defence that can engulf many invading bacteria?
questions.explanation: Phagocytes such as neutrophils and monocytes engulf microbes. Red cells transport gases, platelets aid clotting, and albumin is a plasma protein.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A clot forms at a wound after platelets adhere and aggregate. Which role of platelets does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Platelets adhere at damaged vessels and help initiate haemostasis, the process that limits blood loss and supports clot formation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In the normal cardiac conduction pathway, which structure delays the impulse briefly after it leaves the sinoatrial node?
questions.explanation: The AV node briefly delays conduction, allowing atrial contraction and ventricular filling before the impulse is transmitted through the His–Purkinje system.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which change would most directly increase the oxygen-carrying capacity of a fixed volume of blood?
questions.explanation: Most oxygen in blood is bound to haemoglobin in red cells, so haemoglobin concentration is the direct determinant among these choices.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: During ventricular systole, which event normally occurs on the left side of the heart?
questions.option_a: The mitral valve opens and the aortic valve closes
questions.option_b: The mitral valve closes and the aortic valve opens
questions.option_c: Both the mitral and aortic valves remain open
questions.option_d: The pulmonary veins empty directly into the left ventricle
questions.explanation: As left ventricular pressure rises, the mitral valve closes; when it exceeds aortic pressure, the aortic valve opens and blood is ejected.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person has a low platelet count but a normal red-cell count. Which problem is most likely?
questions.option_a: Reduced oxygen transport as the primary defect
questions.option_d: Loss of electrical conduction in the heart
questions.explanation: Platelets support clot formation, so thrombocytopenia increases bleeding risk; red cells are the principal oxygen carriers.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which path correctly describes blood flow through the right side of the human heart?
questions.option_a: Venae cavae → right atrium → tricuspid valve → right ventricle
questions.option_b: Pulmonary veins → right atrium → mitral valve → right ventricle
questions.option_c: Aorta → right atrium → pulmonary valve → right ventricle
questions.option_d: Venae cavae → right ventricle → tricuspid valve → right atrium
questions.explanation: Systemic venous blood enters the right atrium through the venae cavae, passes the tricuspid valve, and reaches the right ventricle.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why does the pulmonary artery carry blood with less oxygen than the aorta?
questions.option_a: It leaves the right ventricle before blood passes through the lungs
questions.option_b: It receives blood from the left atrium
questions.option_c: It carries lymph rather than blood
questions.option_d: Its wall removes oxygen from haemoglobin
questions.explanation: The right ventricle sends blood to the lungs for gas exchange; the aorta leaves the left ventricle after blood has returned oxygenated from the lungs.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which plasma constituent contributes most directly to maintaining colloid osmotic pressure and transporting many small molecules?
questions.explanation: Albumin is the most abundant plasma protein and contributes strongly to oncotic pressure while binding and transporting various substances.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In double circulation, blood passes through the heart twice during one complete circuit of the body. What is a key advantage of this arrangement in humans?
questions.option_a: It prevents blood from entering the lungs
questions.option_b: It helps keep oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate and supports efficient delivery
questions.option_c: It eliminates the need for capillaries
questions.option_d: It makes the heart pump only once per heartbeat
questions.explanation: The pulmonary and systemic circuits allow separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood and enable suitable pressure for lung and body circulation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
